title: Bipolar Disorder Early Warning Sign Scale
short: Track the frequency and intensity of certain behaviors and feelings over time, to recognise patterns worth discussing with a healthcare professional.

intro.measures: This form can be used to track the frequency and intensity of certain behaviors and feelings over time. It’s important to note that this is not a diagnostic tool, but rather a way to recognize patterns that may warrant a discussion with a healthcare professional.
intro.instructions: For each item, rate the frequency and intensity over the past week on a scale from 0 to 4.

questions.title: Mood Elevation
questions.text: Feeling unusually optimistic, energetic, or irritable.

questions.title: Sleep Disturbances
questions.text: Difficulty falling or staying asleep, or reduced need for sleep.

questions.title: Increased Activity or Restlessness
questions.text: More active than usual, starting multiple new projects.

questions.title: Impulsivity/Risky Behavior
questions.text: Making impulsive decisions, engaging in risky activities.

questions.title: Racing Thoughts
questions.text: Thoughts moving quickly from one idea to another.

questions.title: Difficulty Concentrating
questions.text: Finding it hard to focus or make decisions.

questions.title: Irritability or Agitation
questions.text: Feeling easily annoyed or overreacting to small issues.

questions.title: Social Withdrawal
questions.text: Avoiding social interactions, losing interest in socializing.

questions.title: Changes in Eating Habits
questions.text: Eating significantly more or less than usual.

questions.title: Performance Changes
questions.text: Decline in performance at work or school.

bands.label: Low likelihood
bands.text: Low likelihood of early warning signs.

bands.label: Moderate likelihood
bands.text: Moderate likelihood; monitor and possibly consult a healthcare professional.

bands.label: Higher likelihood
bands.text: Higher likelihood; strongly consider discussing with a healthcare professional.

note: It’s important to note that this is not a diagnostic tool, but rather a way to recognize patterns that may warrant a discussion with a healthcare professional.
